Overexpressed dominant mutants reduce mitochondrial fusion in heterokaryon assays; the effect of endogenous heterozygous expression in patient axons remains unresolved.
Variant-expressing cells and selected patient fibroblasts show altered mitochondrial network shape; the responsible molecular steps and consistency across alleles remain unresolved.
C240Y patient fibroblasts show an oxidative-stress signal that was absent in the studied R120W fibroblasts; this is not a universal dominant-allele response.
Complex I activity is reduced in the studied C240Y fibroblasts; the R120W comparison was not statistically significant, and mediation of human neuropathy is unproven.
Selected patient fibroblasts show reduced complex I-linked ATP synthesis; the variant-to-bioenergetic mechanism and in-vivo axonal consequence remain unresolved.
Transfected cells carrying selected dominant variants are more susceptible to the tested apoptotic challenge; this does not demonstrate spontaneous patient-axon death.
Dominant-family clinical and electrophysiologic findings establish motor involvement; no single cultured mitochondrial readout has been shown to mediate it.
Dominant-family sensory symptoms and electrophysiology establish sensory involvement; the contribution of each proposed mitochondrial mechanism remains unresolved.
The R120W effect is evaluated with JPH1 coexpression in a transformed-cell model; the modifier context and overexpression limit generalization.
Reduced fusion provides an interpretation of the fragmented network in the same expression system; mediator-specific rescue was not demonstrated.
Complex I-linked respiratory impairment can limit substrate-driven ATP synthesis, although the direct enzyme assay and respiration assay have different significance patterns across the two alleles.

nodes.description: A constitutive null model develops motor abnormalities from about three months and reduced CMAP at five months. Fewer healthy anterior-horn motor neurons and later reduced neuromuscular-junction occupancy were reported, but five-month sciatic axon number, size distribution and myelin g-ratio were preserved. Rotarod differences became nonsignificant after nine months. Protein-abundance panels suggest altered metabolism but do not directly measure ATP flux. Complete loss models recessive GDAP1 deficiency and cannot establish the mechanism of a heterozygous dominant allele.

Embryonic motor neurons and adult dorsal-root-ganglion sensory neurons from exon1-null mice were cultured. Altered mitochondrial morphology/distribution and reduced alpha-tubulin acetylation were observed. Fura-2 assays in motor neurons showed lower resting cytosolic calcium and reduced store-operated entry. These culture findings do not directly measure in-vivo calcium, axonal transport velocity or a dominant allele effect.

evidence.snippet: In 8 Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT) families we identified 4 pathogenic heterozygous GDAP1 mutations, 3 of which are novel. Three of the mutations displayed reduced disease penetrance. Disease onset in the affected individuals was variable, ranging from early childhood to adulthood. Disease progression was slow in most patients and overall severity milder than typically seen in autosomal recessive GDAP1 mutations.

nodes.description: Purified recombinant GDAP1 fragments were studied by crystallography, solution scattering and thermal assays in 2022 and 2023. R120W/H123R and several other core substitutions reduce apparent melting temperature while retaining overall folding; R310Q/W in longer fragments instead slightly increase it. None of these constructs includes the transmembrane anchor. These experiments measure protein biophysics, not cellular half-life, mitochondrial fusion or clinical severity.
